sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Blank-Check Entity for Public Market Acquisition Mergers (SPAC)

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: SADC Protocol on Finance and Investment
Double Taxation Agreement between South Africa and the United Kingdom (2017)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FIC Act), 2001 (Act 38 of 2001), as amended by Financial Intelligence Centre Amendment Act, 2017 (Act 1 of 2017) and General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act, 2022 (Act 22 of 2022); Prevention of Organised Crime Act, 1998 (Act 121 of 1998); Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorist and Related Activities Act, 2004 (Act 33 of 2004); Companies Act, 2008 (Act 71 of 2008) sections 12, 33, 170 read with Companies Regulations, 2011 regulation 32 and Companies Amendment Act, 2024 (Act 16 of 2024); FIC Guidance Note 3 of 2023 on Beneficial Ownership

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Passport for Each Director and Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Home Affairs / Notary Public in country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (South Africa is a party to the 1961 Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of Residential Address (Utility Bill or Bank Statement) for Each Director/UBO
Consent to Act as First Director (Notice of Consent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and, if foreign signatory, Hague Apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Ultimate Parent Entity or Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if non-Hague Convention country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated Sanctions List, South African Treasury and Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) terrorist and proliferation financing lists, OFAC SDN list, and UK/EU consolidated sanctions where relevant; Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is required for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP) in compliance with FIC Act sections 28A and 28D and FIC Guidance Note 3 of 2023.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission) e-Services Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or any of the 11 official South African languages using the Latin script; non-Latin script names require a transliteration into Latin letters. The name must comply with Companies Act section 11(1), be distinguishable from existing names on the CIPC register, not be confusingly similar to a registered trademark, and include the obligatory suffix '(Pty) Ltd' for a proprietary limited company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a name reservation, the applicant may file a reconsideration request via the CIPC e-Services portal within 30 days of the rejection notice, supported by a legal memorandum distinguishing the proposed name from cited prior names. If CIPC maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal for a formal review under section 12(3) of the Companies Act read with Companies Regulations, 2011. An approved name reservation may be renewed for a further 180 days by filing a renewal application before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only if it provides a physical street address within South Africa capable of receiving service of process and is not a mere post office box. For a SPAC or blank-check cash shell, banks and regulators will generally expect a permanent physical office accommodating board meetings and record retention; however, a serviced office address from a licensed business centre is acceptable for CIPC registration.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 35% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by CIPC or FIC for a non-operating SPAC shell vehicle with a trust or escrow account, given the elevated money-laundering risk profile and sectoral enforcement campaigns.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as read with the Companies Regulations 2011 (GN R340 in GG 34239); applicable sections: ss 8(1) (private company), 13 (registration requirements), 14 (incorporation process), 19 (legal capacity and limited liability), 40 (issue of shares for consideration), 56 (beneficial ownership), 66 (board appointment), 86 (company secretary), 95-100 (offer of securities); JSE Listings Requirements Chapter 4 (SPAC regime effective 1 July 2021); Financial Markets Act 19 of 2012.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), an agency of the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition, acting through the CIPC e-Services online portal and the Companies Tribunal for name review.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) accompanied by the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI), Declaration by Directors (Form CoR 14.1A) and, where applicable, the Name Reservation Certificate (Form CoR 9.3).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private company under s 19(2) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008; shares may be issued at no-par value with no minimum subscription at incorporation. For a listed SPAC, the JSE SPAC regime requires the substantial majority of gross IPO proceeds (at least 90% per the trust deed, in line with international market practice, subject to JSE listing approval) to be deposited immediately into an independently administered trust/escrow account, held for the benefit of public shareholders, and released only upon a qualifying acquisition approved by shareholder vote (a qualifying acquisition must equal at least 80% of the trust assets) or returned to investors if no acquisition completes within the prescribed period (generally 24 months).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Memorandum of Incorporation and subscriber share applications be ratified, and the allotment and issue of ordinary no-par value shares to subscribers be approved, subscription proceeds to be placed into the designated SPAC trust escrow account pending a qualifying acquisition, per section 40 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office at [address], Johannesburg, be adopted as the company's statutory domicile and address for service. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Name] Company Secretary, each to hold office pursuant to sections 66 and 86 of the Companies Act and the MOI, with authority to open bank and escrow accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the company name with the national registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal (www.cipc.co.za), Companies and Intellectual Property Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form CoR 9.1 through the CIPC e-Services ticketing system, nominating up to three name reservations in order of priority. Pay the prescribed name reservation fee electronically before submission. CIPC screens the proposed name against the company names register and trademarks database. Upon approval, CIPC issues Form CoR 9.3 (Name Reservation Certificate), valid for six calendar months, within which the Company must be incorporated. Use a distinctive SPAC-oriented name that does not imply investment advice without FSCA authorisation.
required_dossiers: Form CoR 9.1 (Application for Reservation of Company Name)
Certified identity documents of the applicant and incorporators
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee
Consent letters for each proposed name if using names of living individuals
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as undesirable or confusingly similar (s 11), the incorporator may file an application for reconsideration with the Companies Tribunal within 20 business days of the notice of refusal under s 160 of the Companies Act, or alternatively reserve an alternative name through a fresh CoR 9.1 submission; upon persistent refusal, incorporate using the company's registration number as the name and later apply to change the name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, execute, and attest the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and first directors; South African corporate counsel for drafting; no notarial attestation required by the Companies Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the bespoke SPAC MOI incorporating, inter alia, the rights attaching to ordinary and founder shares, the escrow and trust undertaking of the promoters, the board composition, and the indemnity provisions required by the JSE SPAC regime. Have each incorporator sign the MOI and Form CoR 14.1 in one or more counterparts; execute Form CoR 14.1A (Declaration by Directors) before a commissioner of oaths. Collate all statutory declarations and circulate to the first board for ratification before lodgement.
required_dossiers: Memorandum of Incorporation (bespoke SPAC MOI)
Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation) signed by each incorporator
Form CoR 14.1A (Declaration by Directors) commissioned by a commissioner of oaths
Certified identity document copies of all incorporators and first directors
Written consent of each named director to act in that capacity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOI contains a defect identified by counsel or CIPC, the incorporators must approve an amending resolution and resubmit the corrected MOI; any limitation provisions contrary to s 15 of the Companies Act must be redrafted before lodgement to avoid rejection under s 14(1).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodge the incorporation filing electronically and pay the prescribed fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal, online company registration module
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log into CIPC e-Services, select Company Registration, attach the completed CoR 14.1, MOI in PDF format and CoR 14.1A, and pay the statutory incorporation fee (approximately USD 35, comprising the R600 non-standard MOI fee and R50 name reservation fee) via EFT or card. CIPC performs the ex ante conformity review and, upon approval, issues the Certificate of Incorporation and a registration number in the format YYYY/XXXXXX/07. Download and archive the certificate, and apply for a Central Supplier Database vendor number if government contracting is anticipated.
required_dossiers: Completed Form CoR 14.1
Memorandum of Incorporation in PDF format
Form CoR 14.1A (Declaration by Directors)
Name Reservation Certificate (Form CoR 9.3)
Proof of incorporation fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC returns a query or rejection, correct the flagged deficiencies in the forms and resubmit within the response window stated in the e-Services dashboard (typically 15 business days); engage a registered CIPC practitioner to clear repeated rejections; no re-payment of the registration fee is required for a purely formal resubmission under the same application reference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-incorporation statutory registrations: SARS, beneficial ownership, and employment funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS eFiling); CIPC (beneficial ownership); Department of Employment and Labour (UIF, COIDA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as a SARS taxpayer via eFiling to obtain an income tax reference number; register for VAT if taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed ZAR 1 million per 12 months; register for PAYE, UIF and SDL (Form EMP101) if employees are engaged. File the beneficial ownership register declaration with CIPC (Form CoR 30.1) within 10 business days of incorporation, reflecting ultimate natural persons holding 5% or more. Complete the COIDA notice of registration with the Compensation Fund. Open the commercial bank and SPAC trust/escrow accounts, presenting FICA-compliant corporate documentation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and MOI
Directors' certified identity documents
SARS registration forms (RAF001, VAT101, EMP101)
Beneficial ownership schedule for Form CoR 30.1
Board resolution for bank and escrow account opening
FICA corporate due-diligence file
COIDA registration form for the Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS issues a verification or objection letter, respond within 21 days via eFiling with corrected supporting records; for beneficial ownership discrepancies, submit an amended CoR 30.1 electronically and settle any applicable late-filing penalty only after review; if COIDA is queried, obtain a formal assessment letter from the Compensation Fund and furnish the approval to the Department of Employment and Labour.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish the SPAC trust/escrow structure and, where applicable, secure JSE and FSCA listing clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) and JSE Limited (Issuer Regulation); licensed South African banking and trust institutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conclude the trust deed appointing an independent registered trust company as trustee of the SPAC escrow account; obtain legal confirmation that the escrow arrangement satisfies the JSE SPAC requirements (minimum trust contribution, release thresholds, and the 24-month acquisition deadline). If the Company intends to list, submit the pre-listing statement and draft prospectus to JSE Limited for review, and file the prospectus with the FSCA in accordance with the Companies Act ss 95-100. If the Company remains a private blank-check vehicle, maintain the escrow account under independent administration and document the AML/CFT risk classification as Medium Risk Enhanced.
required_dossiers: Trust deed for the SPAC escrow account
Board resolution approving the trust arrangement
Certificate of Incorporation and MOI
JSE pre-listing submission and draft prospectus (if listing)
FICA due-diligence file (KYC forms, source of funds declaration)
AML/CFT institutional risk assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JSE or FSCA requires amendments to the trust deed, MOI or prospectus, convene a board meeting to adopt conforming amendments and re-file within the stated review period (generally 20 business days); if the bank rejects the escrow mandate for KYC reasons, substitute another licensed deposit-taking institution and conduct enhanced due diligence on all ultimate beneficial owners before resubmission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) for authorisation and prospectus scrutiny under the Financial Markets Act 19 of 2012 and the Companies Act 71 of 2008 (ss 95-100); JSE Limited (Issuer Regulation) for approval of the SPAC listing under Chapter 4 of the JSE Listings Requirements; South African Reserve Bank for exchange control approval relating to offshore qualifying acquisitions where applicable.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: JSE Approval of the SPAC Listing and FSCA Registration of the Securities Prospectus (Special Purpose Acquisition Company regime effective 1 July 2021 under the JSE Listings Requirements). No FSCA financial services provider licence is required where the vehicle does not render financial advice or intermediary services; a Category I FSP licence is required only if the board undertakes regulated advisory activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE), in conjunction with the relevant provincial environmental department
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the SPAC vehicle performs no listed activity under the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations, 2014 (Listing Notices 1, 2 and 3, GN R326-327 of 7 April 2017); only the general duty of care under s 28 of the National Environmental Management Act 107 of 1998 applies to the registered office leasehold; no environmental authorisation is required for pure financial administration, and a Section 30 incident-reporting obligation applies only in the event of any environmental incident.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to a non-operational financial vehicle: no wastewater discharge, VOC, or combustion emissions are generated; office wastewater must nonetheless comply with municipal sewer by-laws and SANS 10400; general waste disposal must comply with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act 59 of 2008, s 16 duty of care; any hazardous waste arising from an office fit-out must be removed by a registered waste transporter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 clearance certificate following a baseline risk assessment by a registered OHS practitioner; fire safety certificate from the local metropolitan fire services (SANS 10139 and SANS 10400 Part T compliance); structural load and electrical installation certificates for the registered office (SANS 10142); emergency evacuation and first-aid readiness verified by the Department of Employment and Labour; COIDA letter of good standing confirming compensation cover is in force.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) - https://www.sars.gov.za; eFiling portal at https://efiling.sars.gov.za. Exchange control oversight for SPAC trust proceeds is shared with the South African Reserve Bank (SARB) under the Currency and Exchanges Act (Cap. 9).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) For an incorporated SA (Pty) Ltd, the CIPC Companies and Intellectual Property Commission filing auto-creates a SARS income tax reference number via the CIPC-SARS interoperability gateway; thereafter activate an eFiling profile. (2) For a foreign-incorporated SPAC, file Form ITREG at a SARS Domestic Branch or via eFiling for an income tax reference number, attaching certified foreign certificate of incorporation, board resolution, director IDs and Power of Attorney to a nominated SA public officer. (3) Compulsory VAT registration via Form VAT101 within 21 days of exceeding the ZAR 1,000,000 turnover threshold; voluntary VAT101 registration is open when taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 (VAT Act s25(1)). (4) Register for PAYE (EMP/EasyPAYE) and UIF if directors/employees are remunerated. (5) Appoint a public officer resident in SA within one month (Tax Administration Act s246). (6) Obtain a Tax Clearance Certificate (TCS) at SARS eFiling before declaring any dividend, redemption or distribution from the SPAC trust/escrow account.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A SA resident company (incorporated in SA or effectively managed in SA) is taxed on worldwide income; corporate income tax rate is 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2024 (28% prior). Dividends to shareholders attract dividends tax (withholding) at 20%; foreign shareholders may invoke treaty relief. The (Pty) Ltd is not a pass-through entity under SA law; no US-style check-the-box applies. SPAC assets held in a separate escrow/trust account constitute an 'affected trust' or 'SPV' for specific CFC and controlled-company anti-avoidance rules, and the escrow interest is taxable at the company level regardless of distribution. The entity is within the SACU territory export zero-rating system but does not itself qualify as a tax-exempt zone vehicle unless designated under s10(1)(cN) or a binding private ruling is obtained from SARS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa has no check-the-box or fiscal transparency election. Available statutory elections relevant to a SPAC holding and M&A: (1) Headquarter Company status under s9I (elected by meeting 80% gross-income and cost thresholds) exempting foreign dividends, interest, royalties and capital gains on foreign subsidiaries; (2) CFC pooling election under s9D in respect of net income of foreign target companies; (3) Hybrid mismatch recharacterisation rules under s8E, s8F, s8FA and s23H apply ex lege, with an election to apply the 'structured arrangement' safe harbor where intent is documented; (4) Election under the VAT Act s23 to voluntarily register for VAT where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000; (5) Section 64B deemed-dividend election for distributions in specie; (6) Binding Private Ruling (BPR) application to SARS for any novel SPAC trust/escrow or earn-out arrangement; (7) Dividend access and capital redemption elections under the Companies Act affecting the s46/ s44 tax-free roll-over treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS; harmonised within the Southern African Customs Union (SACU) for goods movements.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration at ZAR 1,000,000 of taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months (VAT Act s23(1)); voluntary registration at ZAR 50,000 (s25(1)). For a SPAC, financial intermediation services (active management of escrow, share dealing, dividends) are exempt financial supplies under s12, which do not count toward the threshold; registration is generally not triggered unless the SPAC makes taxable supplies of goods or non-exempt services (e.g., advisory, listing fees not zoned as financial services). Once registered, the SPAC must charge VAT at 15% on taxable supplies and cannot recover input VAT attributable to exempt financial supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping akin to Latin American regimes is currently in force. SARS is phasing in mandatory e-Invoicing for selected large vendors, aligned with the Pan-African e-Invoicing standard and the AfCFTA digital trade protocol, requiring structured XML/UBL invoices transmitted to SARS via an approved Service Provider or direct API. Existing s20(4) statutory tax invoice requirements apply to all VAT vendors: vendor name and VAT number, invoice date, invoice number, description, quantity, unit price, VAT rate, and consideration. SARS cross-matches invoice data at VAT201 return level via eFiling APIs; non-compliant transactions are flagged for audit under the Tax Administration Act (TAA) risk engines. Credit notes must comply with s21 and be issued within 21 days of the event trigger.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0%) applies under s11(1)(a) of the VAT Act to goods supplied and exported from the Republic within 90 days of payment (or such extended period as SARS approves), provided title and risk pass to a non-resident abroad. Section 11(1)(j) zero-rates supplies to foreign-going ships and aircraft; s11(1)(k) zero-rates internationally supplied services and services physically rendered outside SA to non-residents where the recipient is non-resident and the services are not connected to immovable property in SA. A SPAC's own escrow management, merger and acquisition financing services are financial supplies and therefore exempt, not zero-rated; only separate cross-border fee arrangements with non-resident target groups may qualify under s11(1)(k). Documentary proof must show physical export (customs clearing), payment in foreign currency or ZAR from a non-resident source, and the exported goods must be delivered and used overseas. Claims for refund of any excess VAT paid must be made within 5 years of the tax period (s44 TAA) and are subject to data matching with SAD500 customs declarations.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SASAD500 / SAD500 transmitted via Customs EDI or eFiling) reflecting the export and SPAC cargo nature
Bill of Lading (or Airway Bill / Road Consignment Note) evidencing physical movement of goods offshore within the 90-day period
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank-issued IRC or Foreign Exchange Proof) evidencing receipt of export proceeds in ZAR/foreign currency within 180 days
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may raise additional assessments within 5 years of the assessment date, extended to 7 years where a return was omitted or a non-deduction was claimed; unlimited prescription exists for fraud or misrepresentation. Zero-rating claims lacking the SAD500, B/L, IRC evidence bundle are disallowed and VAT clawed back with interest at the prescribed rate (currently SARB repurchase rate plus 3%). Understatement penalties under TAA s222-223 apply as a percentage of the resulting shortfall: 10% for substantial understatement, 25% for no reasonable grounds, 50% for gross negligence, and 150% for intentional tax evasion; the 150% tier triggers automatic criminal referral. Criminal prosecution for fraudulent export zero-rating carries a fine of up to ZAR 30,000 or 24 months' imprisonment per charge (or both). Non-repatriation of export proceeds beyond 180 days is a SARB exchange-control contravention under s9 of the Currency and Exchanges Act, subject to administrative penalties of up to 100% of the under-repatriated amount and possible forfeiture. For SPAC capital held in trust/escrow, SARS applies specific anti-avoidance validation (e.g., s103 TAA general anti-avoidance) when the zero-rating is used to recover VAT on expenditures not linked to genuine export of goods or services.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) - Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) and the Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a dual-tier exchange control regime supervised by SARB FinSurv. Current account transactions are substantially liberalised and may be processed through authorised dealer banks without prior SARB approval. Capital account transactions, including inward equity subscriptions and outward acquisition funding by a SPAC, require documentation of a SARB-issued deal/registration reference or use of the electronic Investment Register. Profit and dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are freely convertible once supported by audited financial statements, tax clearance confirmation, and a properly filed dividend withholding tax declaration; however, the underlying share capital must be duly registered with SARB to evidence the inward leg. Practical hurdles include strict beneficial ownership disclosure, source-of-funds substantiation for sponsor contributions, FIC Act section 28A enhanced due diligence expectations, and the prohibition on using unlicensed offshore escrow custodians for mandated trust proceeds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The historical statutory surrender obligation requiring exporters to convert export proceeds into ZAR within 30 days has been abolished under the revised SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers. Exporters in good standing may retain proceeds in foreign currency accounts, subject to monthly reporting via Form A and the authorised dealer's reconciliation against shipping and invoicing documentation. There is no mandatory conversion ratio for eligible export receipts. For a SPAC, any foreign receipts arising from the disposal of underlying assets or reverse-merger consideration must be reported and reconciled with the SARB-approved deal number; unexplained hard-currency inflows are recharacterised as capital account transactions and trigger FinSurv review and potential FIC suspicious transaction reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (trust custody) and Operational Treasury Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: FirstRand Bank Limited (First National Bank division)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Treasury Account (hedging and liquidity management)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI platforms (e.g., Revolut Business, Wise, Payoneer) are not licensed by SARB as authorised dealers and cannot lawfully hold the SPAC's trust-escrow proceeds or execute domestic ZAR clearing. Their viability is rated Low-Medium and is restricted to ancillary functions such as aggregating sponsor commitments from foreign jurisdictions or making small operational disbursements, provided the funds never touch the onshore regulated trust account. The onshore statutory trust-escrow obligation for a listed SPAC under the JSE Listings Requirements and the Companies Act 71 of 2008 requires custody with a registered bank; any use of an unregulated EMI for mandate-critical escrow funds would constitute a compliance breach and trigger FIC enforcement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The FIC Act permits remote customer due diligence using prescribed electronic identity verification; however, Tier 1 banks almost universally require enhanced in-person or high-assurance video-verified interviews for SPAC vehicles classified as Medium-Risk Enhanced. In practice, at least two directors, including one authorised signatory, must attend an initial interview at the bank's Global Corporate Banking office in Johannesburg or Cape Town; remote onboarding is accepted for additional non-resident directors if they provide notarially certified proofs of identity, tax residence certificates, and bank reference letters. Ultimate beneficial owners of the sponsor cannot be onboarded remotely without independent verification by a FICA-compliant introducer, and the appointment of a locally resident compliance director or a registered company secretary is strongly recommended to satisfy the enhanced custody and accountability requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed trust-escrow structure and opaque UBO chain at SPAC formation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organisational chart covering each intermediate holding vehicle; audited shareholder register (Form CM29/CM30); trust deed or escrow agreement; FATCA and CRS self-certification for each UBO; sworn source-of-wealth declarations; and a legal opinion confirming the SPAC's constitutionality under South African company law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Obscure source of funds for sponsor equity premiums and trust-escrow subscriptions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters from discharging institutions; five years of audited financial statements for each sponsor investor; SWIFT MT103 and MT202 records covering the inbound contribution leg; signed representation letter confirming funds are free of illicit origin; and third-party forensic fund-flow analysis if any investor is domiciled in a high-risk jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP or consolidated sanctions exposure of non-resident sponsors or target-company shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP declarations for every director, UBO, and material funder; independent sanctions screening report against UN, EU, OFAC, and South African consolidated lists; certified passport-style identity verification; and a negative-media due diligence report from a reputable global intelligence provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction-stage red flags arising from the reverse-merger target's jurisdiction or counterparty name matching
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approval in principle issued by SARB FinSurv for the inward listing and subsequent outward acquisition; FIC clearance confirmation where applicable; transaction-specific legal opinion from a South African corporate attorney; and detailed closing-curve documentation aligning the share-purchase agreement with actual settlement wires.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward equity subscriptions from non-resident sponsors must be effected by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 wires through a SARB authorised dealer bank. Each remittance must reference the SARB-issued deal number (inward investment registration), the company registration number, and the remitter's upstream bank reference. The prescribed SARB purpose code for SPAC share subscriptions is 4013 (inward equity participation); convertible loan participations use code 4012 (financial loan). All inbound funds must be matched on the electronic Investment Register or Form A within 30 days, and cumulative variances exceeding ZAR 5 million automatically trigger FIC Act section 28A enhanced due diligence, requiring a documented source-of-funds memorandum and independent verification of each sponsor.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements should be cleared via SWIFT MT103 standard commercial payments for acquisition consideration, sponsor fees, and administrative expenses, and via MT700-series documentary credits for trade-backed settlements involving the target's operating subsidiaries. Distribution of the SPAC trust-escrow to target shareholders at closing must be executed by SWIFT MT103 referencing the share-purchase agreement and the SARB-approved outward transaction; where the outward remittance exceeds the ZAR 15 million threshold, prior FinSurv approval or a specific authorised-dealer dispensation must be obtained. Commercial letters of credit may be issued by the onshore authorised-dealer bank in favour of the overseas beneficiary, with all supporting documents mirroring the wire instruction narratives in the closing agreement to preserve a single, auditable trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts (FEC) with authorised dealer banks for up to 24 months to hedge anticipated USD and EUR exposure created by the escrow appreciation and acquisition consideration

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) structures executed with offshore investment banks, permitted only when hedging genuine ZAR/USD commercial exposure and prohibited for speculative purposes under SARB exchange control rulings

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) and interest-rate swaps through SARB-regulated authorised dealers, subject to documentation of an underlying treasury or acquisition-related exposure and compliance with FSCA derivative conduct standards

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (CoR 39.1 electronic filing) - core secretarial renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), South Africa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation (Company Regulations 19(1)); for a 31 March company, due approximately mid-May of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CIPC late-filing penalty per overdue annual return (approx. ZAR 180-900 / USD 10-49 depending on arrear period); two or more consecutive missed annual returns expose the company to a CIPC deregistration notice and administrative strike-off after the statutory opposition window, causing corporate assets to vest in the State under section 82 of the Companies Act 2008.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (CIPC BO filing pursuant to section 26A)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC central Beneficial Ownership Register (shared with the Financial Intelligence Centre and the South African Reserve Bank Financial Surveillance Department)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in conjunction with the CIPC annual return (anniversary date plus 30 business days); any SPAC share allotment, transfer, conversion, or backstop financing event that alters beneficial ownership must additionally be filed within 9 business days of the transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing creates a CIPC compliance flag and constitutes grounds for deregistration; knowingly false BO particulars are an offence under section 214 of the Companies Act (fine and/or imprisonment up to 10 years) and expose accountable institution senior managers to Financial Intelligence Centre Act administrative fines of up to ZAR 10 million (approx. USD 540,000).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) - final CIT computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the tax year, i.e. by the 12th month following the financial year-end; a 31 March year-end requires filing by 31 March of the following year unless SARS issues an earlier auto-assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: SARS may raise an estimated assessment; late submission attracts administrative non-compliance penalties up to ZAR 250,000 (approx. USD 13,500), interest at the SARS statutory uplift rate, and a 5% monthly late-payment penalty on the unpaid corporate tax; prolonged default leads to criminal prosecution and suspension of tax clearance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provisional Tax Returns (IRP6) - first and second interim instalments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First instalment due on the last business day of the 6th month after the financial year-end; second instalment due on the last business day at the financial year-end; optional third top-up instalment within 6 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 20% underestimation penalty applies if the provisional estimate is less than 80% of the assessed taxable liability; non-submission also incurs monthly late-filing penalties up to ZAR 4,000 (approx. USD 216) per month plus interest at the SARS uplift rate for late settlement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Board-approved Annual Financial Statements (audited or independently reviewed as mandated) tabled to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors and shareholders; where the Public Interest Score is 350 or higher or the MOI requires audit, a copy of the audited AFS is also filed with CIPC concurrently with the annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AFS must be issued within 6 months after the financial year-end (section 30(2) of the Companies Act) and tabled to shareholders within 15 business days of board approval (section 31)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Contravention of sections 30 and 31 is an offence; each director may be liable on conviction to a fine of up to ZAR 1,000,000 (approx. USD 54,000) or 12 months' imprisonment, and shareholders may obtain a court order compelling compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies under section 90(1) of the Companies Act 2008 if (a) the Public Interest Score (PIS) is 350 points or above; (b) the Memorandum of Incorporation prescribes audit; (c) shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights so require; or (d) a regulatory body such as the FSCA or the JSE demands audited statements. A SPAC holding multiple subscriber trust balances in escrow accumulates PIS points for third-party fund providers and creditors and will typically exceed the 350-point audit trigger; at PIS 100-349 the statutory default is independent review, and below 100 audit or review is generally not mandatory unless the MOI or a third-party fiduciary contract requires it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Full IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) as adopted by the Companies Act 2008 and enforced by the Independent Regulatory Board for Auditors (IRBA); South Africa has no separate local GAAP. IFRS for SMEs is legally available only to eligible non-public entities with a PIS below 100, but full IFRS remains the prudent and market-standard framework for a blank-check acquisition vehicle owing to the trust escrow disclosure and JSE or international sponsor expectations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain its own Register of Beneficial Ownership at its registered office and mirror that data on the CIPC central BO platform. Annual confirmation is submitted together with the CIPC annual return within 30 business days of the incorporation anniversary. A mid-year SPAC share transfer, share conversion, or trust-fund substitution that changes the natural persons who ultimately own or control the entity must be filed with CIPC within 9 business days of the transaction; the annual re-confirmation does not cure a mid-year event filing obligation.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - 1,600 per annum (CIPC-accredited registered office, company secretary / compliance agent, annual return preparation, and mail-forwarding services in Johannesburg, Cape Town, or Pretoria)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - 30,000 per annum (Registered Auditor (RA) engagement for a special purpose acquisition company, covering escrow trust reconciliation, intercompany loan notes, IFRS AFS, and CIPC-required audit reporting)
